newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dairy 1997/98 target prices unchanged - CDC.
newsitem.headline: Canada dairy 1997/98 target prices unchanged - CDC.

text.p: The price at which dairy farmers begin to collect federal subsidies was unchanged for industrial milk, butter and skim milk powder in dairy year 1997/98 (Aug/July), Canadian Dairy Commission said.
Target prices for producers of industrial milk will remain unchanged from 1996/97 at C$54.23 per hectolitre of milk containing 3.6 kg of butterfat, the CDC said.

An amount of C$0.12 per hectolitre is added to the target price to cover costs associated with the normal stocks of butter held by the Commission to ensure domestic demand is met and cover administrative costs linked to the CDC's marketing.
Butter returns for producers were left unchanged at C$5.324 per kg as were those for skim milk powder at C$4.203 per kg, the CDC said.
An assumed margin for processors that is incorporatedd into those prices will also stay at C$8.12 per hectolitre.
The federal subsidy that is used to moderate the price of industrial milk products to the consumer is scheduled to be phased out over five years beginning in February 1998.
